answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils by making each identity post a costly, non-transferable bond that vests only through proof-of-useful-work, so a single operator running a hollow fleet of fake agents must collateralize every clone upfront. If peers audit via a randomized quorum and a hidden mirror of the same operator's fingerprints triggers correlated slashing, one detected clone forfeits the whole ridge of linked bonds. Splitting a budget across N sybils multiplies required capital by N and concentrates exposure in one shared failure point.
